text.text: Your brokerage in one place. Follow up with new Leads today, keep each Listing current, and run every Transaction from accepted offer to closing with dated Milestones. Operational tracking only.
Most leads are not ready today. The agent who follows up steadily, with something useful each time, is the one they call when they are.
Call new web and sign-call leads within five minutes when you can; response time decides most online leads. Text if they do not answer, then email.
Buying, selling or both? Timeline? Why now?
Buyers: pre-approved? With which lender? Budget and must-haves? Fill in
Sellers: address, what they owe, what they hope to get, when they need to move.
Are they working with another agent? If they signed with someone, stop.

Filter leads with a follow-up date before today. Each one gets contact this week or a new date with a reason. A lead without a date is a lead nobody owns.
A listing gets its best attention in the first two weeks. Launch it complete, priced right and well presented, or the market marks it down for you.

cells.text: Review feedback and showings with the seller

text.text: One meaningful reduction beats several small ones.

Show the seller the three to five closest sales from the last few months, the active competition and the homes that did not sell. Agree a price and a review date together. Sellers who choose a high price against advice should agree in writing to revisit it at 14 days.
Each offer becomes a transaction row only once accepted. Before that, compare offers on price, financing, earnest money, contingencies and closing date, and present them side by side to the seller.
The hillside cottage on Tamarind Way had two reductions and was withdrawn. Before relisting in spring, the agent plans new photos and a pre-listing inspection so buyers see fewer surprises.
Most deals that fall apart do so at a contingency date nobody was watching. Every date in the contract becomes a milestone the day the contract is accepted.
Add the transaction: listing, client, side, contract price, earnest money, financing, commission rate, acceptance and closing dates.

Add a milestone for every date in the contract: earnest money due, inspection period end, appraisal, loan commitment, title review, final walkthrough, closing.
Use the contract's dates, not this table, for every real deal.

The Corbel Street seller has the inspection report review tomorrow and the repair response due on Friday. The listing agent books a call with the seller this evening.
The commission is earned at closing; the next one starts there too. Most agents' best business comes from past clients and their referrals.

When a past client sends a friend, thank them the same week, personally, whether or not the friend buys. Note the referral on both lead rows so the source report gives past clients credit.
Ask for a review only after the day-7 call shows they are happy, and make it easy with one direct link.
Store the full file as your brokerage and state require, usually for several years. Note on the transaction page where it is stored.
The Larkin Avenue condo buyer closed 40 days ago. The day-30 check-in is overdue; the agent calls this week, asks how the move went and mentions a client event next month.
